verdict: Avoid new pharma/API exposure in Pithampur for now; lend only to profitable, compliance-clean formulation units with verified GST and PF records, and decline labour-stressed or single-customer API converters.
title: Pithampur Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Pithampur pharma unit buys API or bulk drugs, runs formulation, packing and QC lines, and sells to domestic distributors or export buyers.** Cash comes in after dispatch and credit period, not at production, so the plant runs on working capital. **The value sits in regulatory approvals and customer qualification, not in the building.** A unit with a US or EU-approved site and repeat buyers has pricing power; a loan-licence converter selling to one buyer does not. **Capex is heavy and lumpy** — a new line or a USFDA-grade block is a multi-year spend, so check what is already committed before you size a term loan. Collect from customer: capacity, product mix, buyer-wise sales, and current term-debt schedule.

## Where cash actually sits
**Working capital is the real exposure in this industry.** Peer rating reports show high working-capital intensity from elongated receivables and high inventory holding [10], and one mid-size player ran fund-based limits at 40-50% utilisation after earlier 70-90% [9]. **So when a proposal lands, check receivable days and inventory days against the buyer mix; if receivables are stretching while sales are flat, ask why and pull the last twelve months of bank statements.** Rating reports also flag customer concentration as a live risk [8]. **If one buyer is more than a third of sales, ask for the contract and the payment history.**

## What has changed now
**The local signal is weak.** Madhya Pradesh GST collections fell 0.1% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, a 6.2 pp gap [D], and India-wide output is down 2.1% Apr-to-date [D]. **Bank credit is growing 21.6% YoY against that falling output [D], so money is chasing a shrinking base — be the lender who asks for the invoice, not the lender who asks for the balance sheet.** Locally, workers at a Pithampur drug company protested over low wages and PF irregularities in April 2026 [3]; that is a compliance and labour-relations flag, not a demand story. **The counterweight is real:** pharma firms have announced ₹2,246 crore of fresh projects in MP aimed at jobs and exports [2], and Ajanta Pharma is hiring production officers locally [1]. **Note the dates — the investment news is July 2026 and the protest April 2026; both are recent but neither is a current financial statement.**

## Where to grow, and how
**Pursue formulation units with domestic plus export mix, clean PF and ESI records, and a second-generation promoter in the business.** Peer results show the strong end of the market is doing well — Aarti Pharmalabs reported record quarterly revenue of Rs. 613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% [4][6], and RPG Life Sciences is targeting 25% API growth [5] even as its stock fell over 10% after Q2 [7]. **That split is the lesson: quality compounds, weak units get punished.** Structure new limits as cash-flow-backed working capital with a charge on receivables, and take monthly GST returns, PF challans and stock statements. **Avoid units with a single buyer, unpaid PF, or a promoter drawing salary while statutory dues lapse.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the payment behaviour first.** If GST filing slips a month or PF challans go unpaid, stop enhancement and inspect stock. **If receivable days cross the peer benchmark, ask for the buyer ledger and confirm the top three balances.** If electricity consumption falls while sales are reported flat, ask for production records. **If a promoter seeks a second lender for the same receivables, decline.**
watch: filing slips or turnover falls >20% -> freeze enhancement, inspect stock
any month unpaid -> treat as compliance breach, seek explanation in writing
days stretch beyond peer benchmark -> confirm top three balances directly
consumption falls while sales flat -> ask for production records
inflows fall below EMI plus statutory dues -> restructure or exit
